text:
incident-bot: Paging: GPU driver Xid resets spike on fleet tag=prod-inference-eu (hosts: inf-eu-04..inf-eu-08). Correctable ECC and Xid 31/43 observed. Impact: increased container restarts and a small fraction of 2xx->5xxs. Escalation to oncall.

Alex W (oncall): Ack. I'm on it, pulling telemetry. Which service is hitting the most restarts?

Priya S: Looks like route /v1/generate on model redwood-7b-quant is the biggest. CPU fallback traffic is up slightly.

Devon R: Confirming: kernel logs show repeated Xid 31 messages followed by nvidia-mps or driver reset. Example from inf-eu-06:

```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 31, PID 7421, GPU:0 
[ 12345.679012] NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 12345.679100] nvidia-mps: detached client 7421
```

Alex W (oncall): Thanks. Is this limited to one host or a group?

Devon R: It's a correlated wave across that AZ subset (inf-eu-04->08). Telemetry shows correctable ECC counts rising before the Xid resets. Could be thermal or a flaky driver kernel combo.

eng-runtime: Quick mitigation options: 1) Evacuate GPU pods from affected hosts and force a rolling reboot of the host; 2) Switch traffic to dedicated fallback pool (cpu/different-model) using routing policy; 3) Apply temporary cordon/taint to stop scheduling.

Priya S: Customer impact so far: ~2.3% of requests get 5xx within that AZ, latency p95 up 300ms for the affected nodes. A few customer sessions noted truncated responses. No major customers fully blocked yet.

Alex W (oncall): Action plan:
- Immediate: cordon inf-eu-04..08 and drain pods (ignore-daemonsets). Move workloads to fallback lane.
- Medium: reboot nodes after drain and check ECC counts after cold boot.
- If noise persists: failover traffic regionally and open customer bridge.

sre-bot: Runbook link: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-xid-ecc>. Recommended drain command: `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60`.

Alex W (oncall): Starting drains now. Running on inf-eu-04 first.

Priya S: I'll flip routing for /v1/generate to include dedicated-fallback (100ms extra latency but stable).

Devon R: Observed one pod eviction where the container restarted after a driver reset, logs show the runtime crashed with: `RuntimeError: Cuda error: unknown error` then kubelet OOM eviction later. Posting snippet: 

```
2026-03-14T19:22:01Z /app/serve.py: ERROR Cuda error: unknown error
2026-03-14T19:22:02Z kubelet: Killing container with id docker://...: Container failed liveness probe
```

Alex W (oncall): Drain progress: inf-eu-04 drained, inf-eu-05 draining, inf-eu-06 pending - kernel still logging Xid.

eng-runtime: If inf-eu-06 keeps spitting Xids during drain, escalate to host reboot. Also capture dmesg and nv-hostengine logs before reboot (`journalctl -k -u nvidia-persistenced -b`).

Priya S: Routing switch in progress. Will post impact numbers once stable.

(emoji :hourglass_flowing_sand: reaction)

Devon R: Captured nv-hostengine snippet from inf-eu-06 before partial reboot: 
```
Mar 14 19:20:12 inf-eu-06 nvidia: ecc correctable error count: 912 -> 935 within 5m
Mar 14 19:20:15 inf-eu-06 nvidia: Xid 43 at 0x7f8a9b2c
```

Alex W (oncall): Rebooting inf-eu-06 now (scheduled after drain complete).

Priya S: After flipping routing, error rate from that AZ to overall fell from 2.3% -> 0.5% in 10m. Good. Still watching.

eng-runtime: Note: autoscaler might try to spin new pods into the drained nodes if cordon not applied correctly. Please taint nodes `gpu=ecc-flicker:NoSchedule` while investigating.

Alex W (oncall): Applied taint gpu=ecc-flicker:NoSchedule to inf-eu-04..08.

Devon R: inf-eu-06 came back from reboot and initial ECC counters after boot are low, but we see intermittent Xid 31 at boot-time. Kernel driver version is 525.85.12. Suggest rolling the driver to 525.89.01 on the affected pool if we see recurrence.

Priya S: Customer CS flagged 3 sessions with truncated outputs — reached out to customers A and C to explain transient errors and that we're routing to fallback. No escalations yet.

Alex W (oncall): Next steps: keep taint, keep fallback routing for 30m, monitor ECC and Xid metrics. If recurrence > 0.5% error rate, do driver rolling update + scheduled maintenance.

eng-runtime: Patch candidate and canary plan: driver 525.89.01 -> rollout to one node, run synthetic workload for 1h, then broad rollout. Need approval window for node reboots.

Devon R: I've uploaded collected dmesg / nv logs to the incident artifact: <https://redwood.internal/artifacts/4470001111>.

sre-bot: Metric snapshot: error_rate_by_az(prod-inference-eu) = 0.5% (down from 2.3%), node_restarts = 5 in last 15m, ECC_correctables trending down.

Alex W (oncall): Handoff in 25m to Priya (next oncall). Leaving notes: tainted nodes, drains done for 04..05, 06 rebooted, 07/08 scheduled. Route policy set to dedicated-fallback. Follow-up: driver roll test tomorrow.

Priya S: Taking over in 25. I'll keep the client comms and coordinate the driver canary.

Devon R: FYI — we should add a post-incident action to add more granular nv-host metrics into the alerting rule (ECC correctables threshold per-minute) to detect earlier.

Alex W (oncall): Agreed. I'll file a P0->P1 postmortem checklist item. For now marking this thread monitored.

(emoji :white_check_mark: reaction)

Priya S: I'm now the oncall owner. Keeping taint in place for 30m more. Will update thread if anything changes.

sre-bot: Closing automated paging (acknowledged).
